proposedPlacement: After learner reads Deuteronomy 6:4 KJV, as optional brief visual vocabulary support

proposal.title: Why is LORD written in capital letters?
proposal.interaction: Learner selects either occurrence of LORD in the existing KJV verse and sees a short explanation of how English translation typography distinguishes the divine name from the ordinary title lord.
proposal.draftExplanation: In many English Bibles, LORD in capitals represents the Hebrew personal name of Israel's God. This translation convention helps readers recognize whom the Shema confesses. It does not change the biblical truth that the LORD our God is one LORD.
proposal.learnerCheck: In Deuteronomy 6:4, what does the repeated LORD emphasize about the God Israel is commanded to hear and acknowledge?
proposal.teachingLimits: Keep focus on Deuteronomy 6:4, Isaiah 44:6, Isaiah 45:5, and Mark 12:29. This note supports reading the Shema, not a test on Hebrew phonetics, Jewish ritual practices, or divine-name etymology.
